correctness.rationale: The conditional-edge argument lists crossing possibilities \((d-1)(2n-d-1)\), outer nesting possibilities \(\binom{d-1}{2}\), and inner nesting possibilities \((i-1)(2n-j)\), each present with probability \(1/(2n-3)\). The remaining-edge expectation is \((n-1)(n-2)/6\). Elementary piecewise sums give W, UX, UN and both exact mixed covariances. The S variance follows from matching two-edge inclusion probabilities and deterministic endpoint span sums. Crossing variance has a direct four-endpoint indicator moment proof; Kasraoui–Zeng Theorem 1.2 gives equality of crossing and nesting variances. Correlation limits then follow algebraically. Exhaustive enumeration \(2\le n\le7\) and independent weighted sums \(2\le n\le200\) passed 850 exact assertions. Finite tests are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The canonical chord-length function from the probabilistic literature supplies natural geometry, while crossing-pair and nesting-pair counts have exactly the same marginal distribution. Their covariances with total circular span have opposite sign and an exact order-n magnitude ratio. Consequently one standardized correlation tends to sqrt(15)/4 and the other decays as −sqrt(15)/(4n): a structural boundary between geometry and two equidistributed pair patterns, informative beyond reparametrizing known marginals.
